chosenSubject: Ford Model T goes on sale
chosenAngle: How a lower-priced, practical car helped families imagine travel beyond horses, streetcars, and trains
episodeThesis: A machine can change daily life when engineers make it simple, durable, and cheaper for ordinary families to use.
timeline: October 1, 1908: Ford introduces the Model T automobile
1908: The Model T is sold for about $850, still expensive but lower than many luxury cars of the time
1913-1914: Ford's moving assembly line helps reduce production time and pushes Model T prices downward
1927: Ford ends Model T production after building more than 15 million cars
storyBeats: A child in 1908 sees streets where horses, wagons, streetcars, and a few noisy automobiles all share the road
The Model T promises a car sturdy enough for rough roads and simple enough for more people to drive
Its falling price helps explain why cars moved from rare luxury machines toward everyday family transportation
The episode can compare horse-powered travel, early gasoline cars, and today's electric vehicles
modernRelevance: Modern debates about gasoline cars, electric vehicles, city design, traffic, and family mobility still trace back to the moment cars became practical mass-market transportation.
